title: The fibrewise local-complete-intersection locus is open and base-change compatible
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a locally finite type morphism [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Put $s=f(x)$ for $x\in X$, and let $X_s$ denote its scheme-theoretic fibre [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. Let $V_f$ be the set of $x$ such that $\mathcal O_{X_s,x}$ is a complete-intersection local ring over $\kappa(s)$, with the local-ring meaning in [lem-trf-lci-pointwise-criterion]. For every morphism $S'\to S$, write $f':X'=X\times_SS'\to S'$ and $g':X'\to X$ for the base change and projection [def-pc-fibre-product]. Then $V_{f'}=(g')^{-1}(V_f)$. If $f$ is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], then $V_f$ is open. This open is the syntomic locus: it is the largest source open whose restriction is flat, locally of finite presentation, and has local-complete-intersection fibres, where that fibre condition means that every local ring of every fibre is a complete-intersection local ring over its residue base field. Empty fibres and the empty source are allowed.

source.place: Tag 02V3 (lemma-set-points-where-fibres-lci), including its last assertion on the open syntomic locus and its fibre-local-ring definition of the locus.
